title: Translate a Go ParsePort to exceptions
problem: port.py contains a Go function that returns (int, error). Write the Python version: parse_port() returns the port number on success and raises a custom PortError on failure. Keep the original int() error attached as the cause, the way %w wraps an error in Go.
requirements: Define `class PortError(ValueError)` in port.py, so callers that catch ValueError still catch it
parse_port(text) returns an int from 1 to 65535
What counts as a number follows int(): surrounding whitespace is fine (' 443\n' is 443)
Not a number: raise PortError("invalid port <text repr>") chained to the original ValueError with `from`. For example: invalid port 'http'
A number outside 1–65535: raise PortError("port <n> out of range 1-65535"), with no cause. For example: port 0 out of range 1-65535
No print(), no return of None or -1 for errors
contract: class PortError(ValueError); parse_port(text: str) -> int, raises PortError
expectedBehavior: parse_port('8080') == 8080; parse_port(' 443\n') == 443; parse_port('http') raises PortError("invalid port 'http'") whose __cause__ is the ValueError from int(); parse_port('0') raises PortError('port 0 out of range 1-65535')
edgeCases: The limits 1 and 65535 are valid; 0 and 65536 are not
Negative numbers are numbers, so they get the out-of-range message
hints: Conceptual: there are two different failures. One comes from int() (you catch it and re-raise your own error, chained), and one is your own rule (you raise it directly). Go's `if err != nil { return ..., fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err) }` becomes `except ... as err: raise ... from err`.

Specific: the class body can be just `pass`. Put only the int() call inside try, and do the range check after it. The message uses {text!r} for the quoted form ('http'), and a chained comparison 1 <= n <= 65535 works in Python.

Implementation: try: n = int(text) / except ValueError as err: raise PortError(f"invalid port {text!r}") from err. Then: if the number isn't between 1 and 65535, raise PortError with the range message. Otherwise return it.
evaluation: The try block contains only the call that can fail (int)
The range error is raised directly, not from inside an except block
